subject: Copywriting
title: De Beers: A Diamond Is Forever
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on De Beers: A Diamond Is Forever.

hook.text: 'A Diamond Is Forever.' Frances Gerety wrote it in 1947. It's been called the greatest slogan of the 20th century.

buildup.text: Before De Beers' campaign, diamond engagement rings weren't tradition. The copy invented the tradition.

discovery.text: The brilliance: linking diamonds to 'forever' made reselling feel emotionally wrong. You don't sell forever.

twist.text: De Beers also controlled the diamond supply, creating artificial scarcity.

climax.text: De Beers shows that the greatest copy doesn't reflect culture—it creates it. One sentence invented a wedding tradition.

punchline.text: One sentence invented an entire tradition. Copy can create culture.

details.summary: De Beers' 'A Diamond Is Forever' (1947) is recognized as the most successful advertising slogan of the 20th century. details.whyItMatters: De Beers proves that copywriting can create entire markets. One line transformed a commodity stone into an emotional necessity by attaching it to the most powerful human emotion: love.
takeaways: 'A Diamond Is Forever' created the diamond engagement ring tradition
The slogan linked a commodity product to eternal love
One line generated over a century of cultural and commercial impact

faq.question: How did one slogan create the diamond engagement ring tradition?
faq.answer: Before De Beers' campaign, diamond engagement rings were not standard. The slogan framed diamonds as the only worthy symbol of eternal love — making any other choice seem inadequate. Combined with advertising suggesting men should spend two months' salary, the campaign engineered a cultural norm.

faq.question: Is 'A Diamond Is Forever' the most influential slogan ever?
faq.answer: Advertising Age named it the greatest slogan of the 20th century. No other line has so thoroughly changed consumer behavior on a global scale. It created a market, a tradition, and a social expectation — all from four words.
